body.state: I firmly reject discrimination across all aspects of life specifically including education, employment, healthcare, housing, and criminal justice. I'm dedicated to bolstering civil rights safeguards in combating discrimination and prejudice in our daily interactions. I will champion the rights of minorities and marginal communities, including women, people of color, LGBTQIA+ individuals, immigrants, and people with disabilities. I pledge to advocate for the safeguarding of these communities to guarantee equal access to resources, opportunities, and protections necessary for their well-being. Every individual deserves to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality.

body.state: Juliana Bennett: Increasing affordability is the most pressing issue for my district. There are working families in the 76th that are being pushed out of the homes by rising property taxes, and families who can’t even afford baby formula. I plan on addressing this by lowering rent and property taxes; funding our schools; and raising wages. We’ll lower property taxes by 44% and fund our schools with the 17-cent Millionaire Tax, AB 1209.

body.state: Universal Child Allowance For children, we currently have cash benefits in the form of the Earned Income Tax Credit and the Child Tax Credit. However, these programs are means-tested, overly complicated, and exclude far too many children. Amid the COVID pandemic, the government expanded the Child Tax Credit and cut childhood poverty in half. However, a year later, the government allowed that expansion to expire, shamefully doubling childhood poverty again.

body.state: Meet Shaun. Shaun Navarro has been a leader in the community for nearly a decade. As co-chair of Las Vegas DSA, he helped create a monthly mutual aid event for the unhoused community, showing up every last Sunday for 6 years with supplies and volunteers. He helped craft the free brake light clinic, repairing brake lights for free for low income families. He led the charge on Palestine, arranging protests and education years before the horrific events of 2023.

body.state: Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford: I don’t have the typical background of someone who runs for the Assembly. I’ve experienced homelessness, gone without healthcare, and made $2.33 an hour in the food service industry. And as a transgender woman, I know what it feels like to see your basic rights and freedoms come under attack. That perspective is missing from the legislature. I’ve lived the policy failures of our state government.
